style: a lifestyle journal floor plan drawn by hand on textured paper. Outer walls and partition walls in rough, natural black marker; furniture in a finer hand-drawn line. Every line keeps a slight wobble, doubled-back strokes and honest drafting errors. A pale grey square grid over the floor. Rooms are told apart by local colour: pale mint green, cream beige, terracotta orange, sky blue, soft pink and grass green. Colour is laid in with coloured pencil and light markers, keeping the paper grain, visible hatching, uneven fill and a faint scanner shadow. Furniture is drawn as simple, cute, slightly clumsy top-down illustrations, and the rooms are full of small objects that show how this household actually lives: hobbies, a pet corner, storage baskets, smart-home gadgets, everyday clutter mid-use. Key appliances and daily-life spots carry small handwritten Chinese notes joined to the object by a quickly drawn arrow. The whole page reads like an architect's or the owner's own warm, relaxed, detail-rich life proposal in a personal journal — it is about how life will be lived here, not about drafting accuracy.
composition: strict orthographic top-down 2D floor plan, no perspective, no isometric, no 3D. Vertical portrait orientation. The plan fills the frame with even margins of blank textured paper; the room names and the small notes are written into the drawing itself, so no blank band is reserved.
negatives: professional CAD drawing or estate-agent standard floor plan
3D perspective, isometric views, photorealistic or CGI rendering
printed computer typefaces, ruled label boxes, evenly spaced captions
dimension lines, measurement arrows, scale bars, north arrows, engineering symbols, legends
cold minimalism, luxury show-flat polish, glossy gradients
furniture blocking a door opening or a main circulation path
adding rooms, gardens, gyms or walk-in closets that are not in the source plan
